points.why: States X2 alone explains about 60% of the variance and is dominant.
Notes X1 has only 10% alone but 40% total, with ST−S1 = 0.30 matching S2 = 0.28.
Says S1 or one-at-a-time analysis would make X1 look negligible, advises constraining X2 first and not dropping or fixing X1.
Attributes the small mismatches to Monte Carlo estimation error and recommends bootstrap confidence intervals and larger N.
